title: Stop T2 Mac resume from waiting on the Thunderbolt controllers
author: phedoreanu
body:
## Summary

Opening the lid of a T2 MacBook took about 20 s before the lock screen appeared. With `pm_print_times` the kernel's own accounting shows where it goes: `noirq resume of devices complete after 19061 msecs`, of which

```
pcieport 0000:06:00.0  (Titan Ridge upstream, left)   6.16 s
pcieport 0000:7c:00.0  (Titan Ridge upstream, right)  6.09 s
thunderbolt 0000:08:00.0 (NHI)                        2.86 s
thunderbolt 0000:7e:00.0 (NHI)                        2.83 s
```

The two Titan Ridge controllers lose power in deep sleep. On resume the kernel powers them up and waits for their firmware to bring the PCIe switch back (~6 s each), then the connection manager (~3 s each). T2 Macs need `pm_async=off` (enabling it at runtime hung the machine on the next resume), so these waits run one after another on the critical path.

- Ship `default/systemd/system-sleep/t2-thunderbolt`. Before sleep it removes the Titan Ridge upstream ports, so `pci_bridge_wait_for_secondary_bus()` has nothing to wait for. After resume it rescans in the background until the controllers are back, then gives every childless downstream port a secondary bus reset: the integrated xHCI does not answer config cycles after the power cycle until its port is reset.
- Install it from `fix-t2.sh` (mode 755, as #8588 points out `cp -p` would leave it inert) and migrate existing T2 installs.
- Extend `t2-hardware-test.sh` to cover the hook contents, the fresh setup, the migration, its idempotency, and the non-T2 path.

Apple's Thunderbolt `_PS0/_PS3` methods are all gated on `OSDW()`, so there is no ACPI-side help to lean on under Linux.

## Verification

- `bash test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh` (12 passing)
- `./test/all`: only the pre-existing environment failures also present on `quattro` (missing `omarchy-pkgs` checkout, theme-install URL check)
- MacBookPro16,1, linux-t2 7.1.8, Omarchy 4.0.1, five lid-close/open cycles: kernel resume went from 22.3 s to 4.5 s (`ACPI: PM: Low-level resume complete` to `PM: suspend exit`), the lock screen is up about a second and a half after the lid opens, and both Thunderbolt controllers plus their xHCI (with the USB-C rule from #9195 reapplied on bind) are back within a second of resume. The remaining time is amdgpu (1.1 s), the Wi-Fi root port (1.0 s), the efivarfs resync (0.8 s) and CPU re-online (0.9 s).

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# The Titan Ridge Thunderbolt controllers on T2 Macs lose power in deep sleep.
+# Left in place, the kernel resumes them serially and waits about 6 s per
+# controller for its firmware plus about 3 s per NHI, which is most of the 20 s
+# a lid-open takes. Remove them before sleeping so resume has nothing to wait
+# for, then re-enumerate in the background once they have powered back up.
+
+state=/run/omarchy-t2-thunderbolt
+
+titan_ridge_bridges() {
+  local dev
+  for dev in /sys/bus/pci/devices/*; do
+    [[ -r $dev/vendor && $(<"$dev/vendor") == 0x8086 && $(<"$dev/device") == 0x15ea ]] && echo "$dev"
+  done
+}
+
+# Upstream ports sit directly on a CPU/PCH root port.
+tb_upstream_bridges() {
+  local dev parent
+  for dev in $(titan_ridge_bridges); do
+    parent=$(basename "$(readlink -f "$dev/..")")
+    [[ $parent == 0000:00:* ]] && echo "$dev"
+  done
+}
+
+# Downstream ports hang off another Titan Ridge bridge.
+tb_downstream_bridges() {
+  local dev parent
+  for dev in $(titan_ridge_bridges); do
+    parent=$(basename "$(readlink -f "$dev/..")")
+    [[ $parent == 0000:00:* ]] || echo "$dev"
+  done
+}
+
+has_children() {
+  compgen -G "$1/0000:*" >/dev/null
+}
+
+# The integrated xHCI does not answer config cycles after the power cycle until
+# its downstream port is reset (Bridge Control bit 6, secondary bus reset).
+reset_secondary_bus() {
+  local addr=${1##*/} ctl
+  ctl=$(setpci -s "$addr" BRIDGE_CONTROL)
+  setpci -s "$addr" BRIDGE_CONTROL="$(printf '%04x' $(( 0x$ctl | 0x40 )))"
+  sleep 0.01
+  setpci -s "$addr" BRIDGE_CONTROL="$ctl"
+}
+
+case $1 in
+  pre)
+    count=0
+    for dev in $(tb_upstream_bridges); do
+      echo 1 > "$dev/remove" && count=$((count + 1))
+    done
+    # A controller the last resume's rescan has not brought back yet is still
+    # one to bring back. A suspend inside that window must not lower the count
+    # the next resume works from, or the controllers stay off the bus for good.
+    previous=$(cat "$state" 2>/dev/null)
+    [[ $previous =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || previous=0
+    (( count < previous )) && count=$previous
+    echo "$count" > "$state"
+    ;;
+  post)
+    expected=$(cat "$state" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    (( expected > 0 )) || exit 0
+    (
+      for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
+        echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan
+        (( $(tb_upstream_bridges | wc -l) >= expected )) && break
+        sleep 1
+      done
+      sleep 1
+      echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan
+      for dev in $(tb_downstream_bridges); do
+        has_children "$dev" || reset_secondary_bus "$dev"
+      done
+      sleep 1
+      echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan
+    ) &
+    ;;
+esac

@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+echo "Stop T2 Mac resume from waiting on the Thunderbolt controllers"
+
+if ! lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+hook="${OMARCHY_T2_THUNDERBOLT_HOOK:-/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/omarchy-t2-thunderbolt}"
+
+if [[ -x $hook ]]; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# The Thunderbolt controllers lose power in deep sleep and the kernel then
+# spends ~18 s of every resume waiting on them, one after another. The sleep
+# hook takes them out before suspend and re-enumerates them after.
+sudo install -Dm755 "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/t2-thunderbolt" "$hook"

@@ -7,6 +7,8 @@ source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
 fix_t2="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh"
 other_packages="$ROOT/install/omarchy-other.packages"
 migration="$ROOT/migrations/1785944594.sh"
+tb_hook="$ROOT/default/systemd/system-sleep/t2-thunderbolt"
+tb_migration="$ROOT/migrations/1788110186.sh"
 
 grep -Fq 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" intel_iommu=on iommu=pt pm_async=off mem_sleep_default=deep"' "$fix_t2" ||
   fail "T2 setup installs the suspend kernel parameters"
@@ -20,6 +22,17 @@ grep -Fq 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" intel_iommu=on iommu=pt pm_async=off mem_sl
   fail "T2 setup leaves optional Touch Bar customization uninstalled"
 ! grep -qx 'tiny-dfr' "$other_packages" ||
   fail "the ISO no longer caches tiny-dfr"
+grep -Fq 'install -Dm755 "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/t2-thunderbolt"' "$fix_t2" ||
+  fail "T2 setup installs the Thunderbolt sleep hook executable"
+[[ -x $tb_hook ]] || fail "the Thunderbolt sleep hook is tracked executable"
+grep -Fq 'echo 1 > "$dev/remove"' "$tb_hook" ||
+  fail "the Thunderbolt sleep hook removes the controllers before sleep"
+grep -Fq 'echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan' "$tb_hook" ||
+  fail "the Thunderbolt sleep hook re-enumerates the controllers after resume"
+grep -Fq 'BRIDGE_CONTROL' "$tb_hook" ||
+  fail "the Thunderbolt sleep hook resets childless downstream ports for the xHCI"
+grep -Fq '(( count < previous )) && count=$previous' "$tb_hook" ||
+  fail "the Thunderbolt sleep hook keeps the controller count across back-to-back suspends"
 pass "fresh T2 setup uses t2bce-compatible suspend, fan, and Touch Bar defaults"
 
 test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
@@ -212,3 +225,44 @@ grep -Fxq 'limine-mkinitcpio' "$calls" ||
   fail "T2 rerun migration rebuilds the boot image"
 [[ -f $repair_marker ]] || fail "T2 rerun migration records the machine-wide repair"
 pass "T2 rerun migration repairs installs the broken hardware check skipped"
+
+tb_hook_target="$test_tmp/system-sleep/omarchy-t2-thunderbolt"
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/system-sleep"
+: >"$calls"
+
+PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+  TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+  T2_HARDWARE=1 \
+  OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+  OMARCHY_T2_THUNDERBOLT_HOOK="$tb_hook_target" \
+  bash -euo pipefail "$tb_migration" >/dev/null
+
+cmp -s "$tb_hook" "$tb_hook_target" || fail "T2 Thunderbolt migration installs the shipped sleep hook"
+[[ -x $tb_hook_target ]] || fail "T2 Thunderbolt migration installs the hook executable"
+pass "T2 Thunderbolt migration installs the sleep hook on existing installs"
+
+: >"$calls"
+
+PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+  TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+  T2_HARDWARE=1 \
+  OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+  OMARCHY_T2_THUNDERBOLT_HOOK="$tb_hook_target" \
+  bash -euo pipefail "$tb_migration" >/dev/null
+
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "an already repaired T2 install is left unchanged" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "T2 Thunderbolt migration is idempotent"
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/system-sleep"
+: >"$calls"
+
+PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+  TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+  T2_HARDWARE=0 \
+  OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+  OMARCHY_T2_THUNDERBOLT_HOOK="$tb_hook_target" \
+  bash -euo pipefail "$tb_migration" >/dev/null
+
+[[ ! -e $tb_hook_target ]] || fail "non-T2 systems get no Thunderbolt sleep hook"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "non-T2 systems skip the Thunderbolt repair" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "T2 Thunderbolt migration skips unrelated hardware"
